revisions.correction: Replace the double-bit-looking head with one unmistakable practical single-bit war-axe head. It may have a small blunt poll, but no second cutting edge. Keep the F-rank Bronze construction plain and modest.
Use a clearly round, workmanlike Iron shield silhouette so it cannot be mistaken for the Bronze heater shield. Keep E-rank decoration minimal and preserve the iron surface language.
Use a compact rectangular or softly squared Steel shield silhouette, visibly distinct from both the Bronze heater and round Iron shields. Keep it refined but restrained at D rank.

Create a distinct celestial Starmetal shield outline with an elegant asymmetric star-point or crescent influence. Do not reuse the open oval Skyiron silhouette; preserve A-rank readability and starlit material behavior.

Make the Steel sword a refined hand-and-a-half longsword with a longer blade, a clearly shaped fuller, and a more authored guard than the Iron sword. It must remain practical D-rank steel, not magical.

Give the Starmetal mace a distinctive angular star-flanged striking head and authored A-rank proportions, visibly different from the slim Skyiron mace while preserving mace recognition and controlled starlit detail.

Push the S-rank silhouette into a singular radiant solar sword: a bolder authored blade profile, sunburst guard, and controlled luminous edge. It must be unmistakably above Starmetal at phone scale while remaining a sword.
Create an unmistakable S-rank sunlance spearhead with a longer central point and restrained winged solar geometry. Keep one primary spear point, not a trident, and preserve the long functional shaft.

Create a dramatic but unmistakably single-bit Sunsteel war-axe with one sweeping radiant cutting edge, a small non-cutting counterspike, and an apex S-rank silhouette. Do not make a mirrored or double-bit head.
